solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Service providers in Scottish town protected by those in charge (3,7)

indicatorNotes.protected by: the town is sheltered inside the other word, which wraps round it

blocks.note: Ayr, a town on the Scottish west coast
the people in charge; this word wraps round the town, after its first letter

annotation.surface: A Scottish town's services are run under the eye of the local bosses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service providers' sounds like utilities, but the services are church services: lay readers are non-clergy who lead them.
annotation.definitionFit: Lay readers are laypeople licensed to conduct church services, so they literally provide services.

entries.clue: I distract elk roaming in national park (4,8)

indicatorNotes.roaming: the letters wander about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of drawing the attention of an elk wandering through a national park.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a national park in Cumbria, north-west England, famous for its lakes and fells.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Cumbrian region is one of the national parks of England and Wales.

entries.clue: I agree to eat a starter of toasted fungus (5)

indicatorNotes.to eat: YES swallows the A, so it ends up inside
indicatorNotes.starter of: the starter is the first letter

blocks.note: 'yes' is what you say when you agree

annotation.surface: An enthusiastic diner agrees to try a toasted mushroom starter.
annotation.walkthrough: The meal picture hides a baker's ingredient: yeast is a single-celled fungus.
annotation.definitionFit: Yeast is a microscopic fungus used in baking and brewing.

entries.clue: Before and after evening drinks (3)

indicatorNotes.drinks: the phrase swallows the answer, holding it inside

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'after' plus the first of 'evening'

annotation.surface: A note of drinks served before and after an evening meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before and after' reads as a pair of times, but only 'Before' is the definition; 'after' starts the phrase that holds the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though an old-fashioned, poetic one, as in 'ere long'.

entries.clue: Calling briefly for leather protector (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: DUBBING (calling, naming) without its final G

annotation.surface: Someone phones up quickly to order some leather polish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like a phone call; here it is naming, as in to dub someone a knight. Dubbin is a grease used to waterproof leather boots.
annotation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a wax-and-oil dressing rubbed into leather to soften and waterproof it.

entries.clue: Helen rips pants and top up (9)

indicatorNotes.pants: British slang for rubbish: the letters are a mess

annotation.surface: Helen tears her trousers and her shirt in a wardrobe mishap.
annotation.walkthrough: Pants and top look like clothes; 'pants' is the British slang for rubbish, and 'top up' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To replenish something is to fill it up again, or top it up.

entries.clue: Bad behaviour when driving to Leeds, perhaps, is illusion (6)

blocks.note: the M1 motorway runs from London to Leeds; the 1 is written as I
road rage, the bad temper of drivers

annotation.surface: Road rage on the way to Leeds turns out to be a trick of the mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read the digit 1 as the letter I. Blocks run in answer order, so M1 comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen on a hot road.

entries.clue: A politician affected by temperature on stage (12)

blocks.note: hit = affected, as in 'hit by the cuts'

annotation.surface: An MP on a platform is sweating under the hot lights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage' reads as a platform for the politician, but it is the definition: an amphitheatre is an arena for performance.
annotation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open-air arena or stage where performances are held.

entries.clue: Jack delivered part of church (5)

indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered, so the words are spoken

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church; add a silent K and the sound is unchanged

annotation.surface: A man called Jack brought round a section of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: In playing cards the jack is also called the knave.
annotation.definitionFit: Knave is the older name for the jack in a pack of cards.

entries.clue: Bishop is primarily made to take appropriate sacrament (7)

indicatorNotes.primarily: first and foremost: just the first letter

blocks.note: apt = appropriate; taken in after B

annotation.surface: A bishop is obliged to receive the right sacrament.
annotation.walkthrough: Bishop, sacrament: the church setting is real, and the answer fits it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the rite of christening is one of the Christian sacraments.

entries.clue: Resolve to put off excavation (9)

annotation.surface: Someone decides to postpone digging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as postpone, but the wordplay wants its other sense, discourage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to resolve on something is to decide it firmly.

entries.clue: Gang fight with a sword put to one side (4-5)

blocks.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring

annotation.surface: A street gang settles a quarrel with a sword before putting it away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put to one side' seems to be the sword being laid down; it is the definition, as money is ring-fenced for one purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: To ring-fence funds is to set them aside so they can be used only for one purpose.

entries.clue: Tree has changed (3)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters are altered into a new order

annotation.surface: A tree has altered, perhaps with the seasons.
annotation.walkthrough: A three-letter anagram is short enough to try every order; the definition sits first.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a common European tree with winged seeds.

entries.clue: Hairdresser’s in small town on a regular basis (5)

indicatorNotes.on a regular basis: take letters at regular intervals: every other one

blocks.note: S m A l L t O w N: the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters

annotation.surface: A hairdresser's in a little town that people visit regularly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hairdresser's' is short for hairdresser's shop, so it matches a salon; 'on' belongs to the indicator, not the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The possessive stands for the shop, as in 'going to the hairdresser's', which is the premises where hair is styled.

entries.clue: Spread foam over someone using metalworking tool? (6)

blocks.note: to cover with soapy froth, as a barber does before a shave
the tool is a lathe; add -ER for the person working it, as baker from bake

annotation.surface: A barber soaps a customer's face, or a workshop hand at the lathe.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading is invented: LATHE plus -ER, like a baker or a miner, and the question mark owns up to it.
annotation.definitionFit: To lather is to spread foam; a 'lather' is jokingly one who uses a lathe.

entries.clue: Starting late, winter is unsettled still (5)

indicatorNotes.Starting late: the word begins a letter late, losing its first letter
indicatorNotes.unsettled: the letters are disturbed into a new order

annotation.surface: The weather report: winter has come late and is still changeable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' at the end looks like an adverb, 'is still unsettled'; it is the definition, meaning motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: Inert means still, without motion.

entries.clue: Harry, after taking coat, is in French nick (6)

indicatorNotes.after taking coat: once its coat is taken off, the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: HARRY without its outer letters H and Y

annotation.surface: Prince Harry, having taken someone's coat, ends up in a French police cell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for arrest (and also for a police station, which the surface leans on).
annotation.definitionFit: To nick someone is British slang for to arrest them.

entries.clue: Part of brutal routine (3)

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is a piece of the next word

blocks.note: the second, third and fourth letters

annotation.surface: A grim description of a harsh daily grind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of brutal routine' reads as one phrase; 'Part of' governs only 'brutal', and 'routine' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being stuck in a groove worn by wheels stands for a dull, unchanging routine.

entries.clue: Grange Hill’s opening bores distant timid individual (9)

indicatorNotes.opening: the opening is the first letter
indicatorNotes.bores: H drills into MOUSE, ending up inside it

blocks.note: a timid person is a mouse
first letter of Hill, bored into MOUSE: M(H)OUSE

annotation.surface: The opening episode of Grange Hill bores a shy, far-off viewer.
annotation.walkthrough: Grange Hill was a long-running British children's TV drama set in a school; split off 'Grange' and it is a country house with farm buildings.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, chiefly British: a country house with farm buildings attached.

entries.clue: Civic headwear scratches head (5)

indicatorNotes.scratches head: the head, the first letter, is scratched out

annotation.surface: A mayor's ceremonial hat makes its wearer's head itch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Civic headwear' reads as one phrase, a mayor's hat; the definition is 'Civic' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Civic and urban both mean belonging to a city or town.

entries.clue: Disinfect lists in church (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a ship lists when it tilts to one side; this sits between C and E

annotation.surface: Instructions to sanitise the lists posted up in a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like a noun for rosters; here it is a verb, leans to one side.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to rid something of dirt or germs.

entries.clue: Taxi returned to Italian explorer (5)

indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: as written, then turned round to OT

annotation.surface: A taxi drops a passenger back at the house of an Italian explorer.
annotation.walkthrough: John Cabot was a Venetian navigator who sailed for England and reached North America in 1497.
annotation.definitionFit: John Cabot (Giovanni Caboto) was an Italian explorer.

entries.clue: Company left in depression (3)

annotation.surface: A firm is left in a slump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests an economic slump for the company; it is a dip in a mountain ridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A col is a low point, or depression, in a ridge between two peaks.

entries.clue: Plague pees client off (10)

indicatorNotes.off: gone off, spoiled: the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A pest annoys a customer until they leave in disgust.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plague' reads as a verb, to pester; the answer is the noun, a deadly epidemic.
annotation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, a plague.
